subject: biology-1
question: Plant leaves and bird feathers are covered by a coating that repels water and slows drying. The coating consists of **waxes**. Which property of waxes makes them so effective at waterproofing?

options.text: Long chains of amino acids that crosslink into tough fibers.
Long fatty acid chains linked to alcohols make the coating extremely water-repelling.
Short sugar chains that crystallize into a dry shell.
Ring-structured hormones that seal the outer surface.

explanation: Waxes are lipids built from long fatty acid chains linked to long-chain alcohols, and their extreme hydrophobicity creates the impermeable coatings seen on leaves and feathers. A, C, and D name molecule classes that do not form these surface coatings.
